title: Dominic and the Lantern
premise: In 1890s port town of Saltmere, Rosalind Underhill, indentured to the Corvane Trading Company since childhood, has survived by being unremarkable — until the seasonal bridge closure traps her inside the company compound with a wounded stranger: Ilya Voss, a diver from the rival fleet now declared an enemy of the trade accord, to whom her late father once promised safe passage. Hiding him in the lantern room where she tends the harbor light, Rosalind must choose between the only security she's ever known and a debt of honor no court would recognize. When the company's ruthless factor discovers the truth and offers her freedom in exchange for betrayal, she instead engineers Ilya's escape across the frozen shallows at night — and in doing so, claims a new identity for herself as the keeper of the lantern, no longer invisible but finally her own.
about_author: Kestrel Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing shipping ledgers from coastal trading towns, where the margins told truer stories than the entries. They write historical fiction about people history forgot to record.

chapters.title: The Season of Closed Roads
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. As winter closes the bridge, Rosalind works the counting house, invisible among clerks who never learn her name. She finds a wounded man in the boathouse — Ilya Voss, her father's old diving partner, carrying a letter bearing her father's seal promising shelter. The beat: dread mixed with a strange, unwelcome recognition that her careful invisibility has just become impossible.

chapters.title: What the Lantern Sees
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She hides Ilya in the abandoned harbor lantern room, smuggling food and medicine while the factor, Mr. Grell, tightens his searches after reports of a spy. Through Ilya's stories, she learns her father died not of fever but in a company-ordered dive gone wrong — covered up. The beat: grief curdling into resolve; justice outside the law begins to feel like the only kind available.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, with a tense midpoint shift to Grell discovering a bloodied bandage. Grell corners Rosalind: betray the fugitive and receive her indenture papers torn up, or hang beside him as a traitor. She stalls, signs nothing, and realizes he suspects everything already. The beat: terror transmuting into clarity — freedom bought with another person's life would just be a different cage.

chapters.title: Across the Frozen Shallows
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. During the solstice festival, when every eye is on the company's feast, Rosalind lights the lantern early to draw the watch to the tower, then leads Ilya across the ice at low tide under cover of fog. He begs her to come; she refuses — her fight is here. She returns to face Grell holding proof of her father's death, and the chapter closes with her signing her own name boldly for the first time. The beat: from hidden to seen.
